status_summary: Executive Order 14182 (signed 2025-01-24) states a policy of ending the use of federal taxpayer dollars to fund or promote elective abortion, revokes EO 14076 and EO 14079, and directs OMB to issue implementing guidance; it does not name DOD. A memorandum of 2025-02-03 from the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness, titled Non-Covered Assisted Reproductive Technology, is reported through an earlier browser retrieval of a file that could not be opened in the latest review to rescind the 2023-02-16 USD(P&R) memorandum on administrative absence for non-covered reproductive health care and the Joint Travel Regulations travel policy for that care (paragraph 033113), while preserving access to non-covered assisted reproductive technology (ART) such as IVF. The Acting Secretary of the Air Force's memorandum of 2025-03-17, read on af.mil, implements the order and that memorandum for the Department of the Air Force: it rescinds the Air Force memorandum of 2023-02-27, ends administrative leave and travel and transportation reimbursement for elective abortion effective immediately, and keeps administrative absence and Joint Travel Regulations travel allowances available for non-covered ART. News reports of late January 2025 describe an earlier Pentagon memorandum, signed 2025-01-29, ending the October 2022 travel reimbursement policy; the Army and Navy implementing documents were not read, and the sources show no statute or rule making the change permanent.

timeline.event: EO 14182 signed, stating a policy of ending federal taxpayer funding of elective abortion, revoking EO 14076 and EO 14079 and directing OMB guidance.

The Associated Press reports (published 2025-01-31) that a Defense Department memorandum signed on the Wednesday of that week (2025-01-29 by inference from the weekday; the report gives no calendar date) by the director of the Pentagon's human resources department ends reimbursement for service members' out-of-state travel for reproductive health care, including abortion and fertility treatment, rescinding the October 2022 policy.
Military.com reports the Defense Travel Management Office updated travel regulations, citing the executive order, so travel for abortion and fertility care is no longer reimbursable.

The Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness issued the memorandum Non-Covered Assisted Reproductive Technology, rescinding the 2023-02-16 USD(P&R) memorandum on administrative absence for non-covered reproductive health care and directing the Defense Human Resources Activity to rescind Joint Travel Regulations paragraph 033113 on travel for that care, while stating that access to non-covered ART such as IVF is preserved (read as an attachment to the Air Force memorandum of 2025-03-17, pages 4 to 5).
timeline.source: Department of the Air Force (attached OUSD(P&R) memorandum)

timeline.event: The Acting Secretary of the Air Force signed the memorandum Non-Covered Assisted Reproductive Technology, implementing EO 14182 and the OUSD(P&R) memorandum of 2025-02-03: it rescinds the 2023-02-27 Air Force memorandum, ends administrative leave and travel and transportation reimbursement for elective abortion effective immediately, and preserves access to non-covered ART through a request process for administrative absence and Joint Travel Regulations travel allowances when the care is not available locally.

At a House Appropriations hearing on the FY2026 defense appropriations bill, an amendment to reinstate the 2022 Defense Department policy on travel reimbursement and leave for abortion was voted down.

title: End DOD funding of travel and leave for service member abortions
uncertainties: The Air Force memorandum of 2025-03-17 was opened on 2026-10-19 as a 2-page copy on af.mil (by the researcher, confirmed by the reviewer); it confirms its date, signer, references to EO 14182 and the OUSD(P&R) memorandum of 2025-02-03, the rescission of the 2023-02-27 Air Force memorandum, the end of administrative leave and travel reimbursement for elective abortion, and continued ART access. The 11-page file on the Air Force Medicine site, which also bundles the OUSD(P&R) memorandum, could not be opened (it failed again on 2026-10-26), and the copy of the OUSD(P&R) memorandum on the war.gov host was blocked, so the memorandum itself has not been read. Its rescission of the 2023-02-16 memorandum is stated in the Defense Travel Management Office's JTR change UTD for MAP 08-25(I) of 2025-02-04 (copy on af.mil), which also says the change is not an elimination of access to non-covered ART and that the changes were published in the 2025-03-01 JTR edition. The 21-day limit per request and the closest-available-facility limit on ART travel are confirmed for the Marine Corps by MARADMIN 132/25 (marines.mil, 2025-03-17). The rescission of JTR paragraph 033113 was not confirmed in any opened document; an undated af.mil news article on a Department of the Air Force memorandum of Jan. 29 prints the paragraph as 033013. Coast Guard ALCOAST 087/25 (uscg.mil, 2025-02-25) cites EO 14182 and the OUSD(P&R) memorandum in removing administrative absence for non-covered reproductive health care and reestablishing it for non-covered ART; the Coast Guard is part of DHS, not DOD, so the message shows the memorandum's reach rather than a DOD component's implementation. The Air Force and Marine Corps implementations are documented; the Army and Navy (other than Marine Corps) implementing documents were not read. CRS Insight IN12512 (congress.gov, 2025-02-24) dates to 2025-01-29 the JTR update removing travel and transportation allowances established under the prior administration, and to 2025-02-04 the update reestablishing them for lawfully available non-covered ART; the JTR updates themselves, which CRS links on media.defense.gov, were not opened. The 2025-01-29 memorandum reported by AP, which ended the October 2022 travel reimbursement policy, was not read; the 2025-01-29 date now rests on CRS rather than on inference from the AP report's weekday, and the rescission date of 2025-01-30 reported by the Center for Reproductive Rights (reproductiverights.org, an advocacy group) is an unverified lead at low confidence, not confirmed by an official document. The earlier conflict between sources on fertility care is resolved: the Air Force memorandum, the JTR change of 2025-02-04 and MARADMIN 132/25 keep ART access and travel allowances while leave and travel reimbursement for elective abortion ended; CRS indicates ART travel allowances were removed on 2025-01-29 and reestablished on 2025-02-04, and whether any fertility travel went unreimbursed in that interval was not determined. The Military.com article carries no date in its text; the date is from its URL. Whether military health coverage of abortion under existing law changed was not examined.
